> **The forgetting curve**
> 
> In the 1880s a German psychologist, Hermann Ebbinghaus, carried out an unusual experiment on himself. He memorised long lists of meaningless syllables and then tested how much he could recall after various intervals. The results produced what is now called the forgetting curve: memory declines steeply in the first day and then far more slowly.
> 
> The finding has been repeated many times and is one of the most reliable in psychology. Its practical consequence, however, was ignored by education systems for more than a century. Most courses are still organised in blocks: a topic is taught intensively for a fortnight, tested, and then abandoned. This is almost the opposite of what the evidence recommends.
> 
> The alternative, spaced repetition, involves returning to material at increasing intervals — after a day, then three days, then a week, then a month. Studies consistently find that students using this method retain considerably more after six months than those who study the same total number of hours in a single block. The effect is not small: in several trials, retention roughly doubled.
> 
> Why has adoption been so slow? Part of the answer is that spaced repetition feels less effective while you are doing it. Returning to half-forgotten material is uncomfortable, and progress seems slower than during an intensive block. Learners therefore tend to prefer the method that produces worse results but feels more productive.

**True / False / Not Given (7–10):**
7. Ebbinghaus tested his memory using meaningful words.
8. Most courses today are organised in intensive blocks.
9. Spaced repetition roughly doubled retention in several trials.
10. Ebbinghaus recommended spaced repetition himself.

**Hoàn thành câu (11–14):**
11. Memory declines most steeply during the first ____________.
12. Spaced repetition means returning to material at ____________ intervals.
13. Studies measured retention after ____________ months.
14. Learners avoid the method because it feels less ____________.

writing.de_tom_tat: Task 2, ≥250 từ, 40 phút: University education should be free for all students. To what extent do you agree?
writing.bai_mau:
It is sometimes argued that higher education ought to be provided free of charge to every student. While I accept that cost should never be the reason a capable student is excluded, I believe a fully free system would be neither affordable nor fair.

The strongest argument for free tuition is equality of opportunity. At present, talented students from low-income families often abandon their studies simply because they cannot afford the fees. This represents a considerable waste of human potential. Furthermore, graduates tend to earn more and therefore pay more tax, which means the state eventually recovers much of its investment.

However, there are serious practical objections. University education is expensive to deliver, and the money would have to come from general taxation. This would mean that people who never attend university, including many low earners, would subsidise those who do and who subsequently earn more. In addition, if places were free, demand would rise sharply, and institutions might respond by lowering standards or reducing contact hours.

A more effective approach, in my view, would be targeted support. Tuition could remain payable in principle, but means-tested grants and income-contingent loans would ensure that nobody is prevented from studying by financial circumstances. Under such a system, repayment would begin only once a graduate earns above a defined threshold.

In conclusion, although the aim behind free university education is admirable, I would argue that a well-designed system of grants and deferred repayment achieves the same objective at a far lower cost to society as a whole.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Trả lời trực tiếp "to what extent" bằng quan điểm rõ ở mở bài, giữ nhất quán suốt bài, và đưa ra hướng thứ ba (hỗ trợ có mục tiêu) thay vì chỉ chọn đồng ý hoặc không. Kết luận nhắc lại quan điểm.
Bốn đoạn thân bài rõ chức năng: ủng hộ → phản đối → giải pháp → kết. Từ nối đa dạng và đúng chỗ: Furthermore · However · In addition · A more effective approach · In conclusion.
Từ vựng học thuật đúng ngữ cảnh: free of charge · equality of opportunity · human potential · general taxation · subsidise · means-tested grants · income-contingent loans · defined threshold.

Bị động (is sometimes argued, would be provided) · điều kiện loại 2 (if places were free, demand would rise) · mệnh đề quan hệ (which means the state recovers) · mệnh đề nhượng bộ (While I accept that…, although the aim…).

dang_hoc: Mở bài 2 câu là đủ: paraphrase đề + nêu quan điểm. Đừng viết dài, để dành từ cho thân bài.
Hướng thứ ba ("targeted support") gần như luôn cho điểm Task Response cao hơn việc chọn cực đoan một phía.
Mỗi đoạn thân bài: câu chủ đề → giải thích → ví dụ/hệ quả. Ba lớp là đủ, đừng dồn quá nhiều ý.
"I would argue that…" nghe học thuật hơn "I think" rất nhiều.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ Viết dưới 250 từ → bị trừ điểm tự động, dù nội dung tốt đến đâu.
❌ Mở bài chép nguyên đề → phải paraphrase, không thì phần đó không được tính vào số từ.
❌ Nêu quan điểm ở kết bài mới → phải nêu ngay ở mở bài.
❌ Dùng "Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly" máy móc cả bài → nghe như danh sách, không phải lập luận.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Part 1 — Education: Did you enjoy school? / What was your favourite subject? / Do you plan to study again?

cau_tra_loi.mau: Parts of it, yes. I liked the subjects that involved problem-solving, but I found rote learning quite tedious. Looking back, I wish there had been more practical work.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "Parts of it, yes" — trả lời có sắc thái, hay hơn yes/no. Kết bằng "I wish there had been…" nâng điểm ngữ pháp.

cau_tra_loi.mau: Statistics, oddly enough. At the time I didn't appreciate it, but it turned out to be the most useful thing I studied — I use it almost daily now.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "oddly enough" và "it turned out to be" là cụm khẩu ngữ tự nhiên, thể hiện vốn từ.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Do you plan to study again?
cau_tra_loi.mau: I do, actually. I'm considering a master's programme in technology management. The main obstacle is time rather than money, since I work full-time.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "I do, actually" — dùng do để nhấn mạnh. "rather than" so sánh hai yếu tố.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Câu trả lời có mở rộng tự nhiên, không cụt, dùng câu đệm hợp lý.
rote learning · tedious · appreciate · obstacle · full-time.
I wish there had been (wish + quá khứ hoàn thành) · it turned out to be · rather than.
tedious /ˈtiːdiəs/ · statistics /stəˈtɪstɪks/ trọng âm giữa · obstacle /ˈɒbstəkl/.

meo_noi: Part 1 chỉ cần 20–30 giây mỗi câu. Đừng nói quá dài, giám khảo sẽ cắt.
Luôn có một chi tiết cụ thể ("Statistics", "technology management") — trả lời chung chung mất điểm.
"oddly enough", "looking back", "actually" — bộ câu đệm tự nhiên, dùng xen vào.
